Name: SDV-Radiance
Author: PHUICMT
Description:
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/49397/49397-1791090240-1622644431.jpg[/img]

[size=4][b]Light, shadow, water and weather for Stardew Valley, drawn on top of the frame your game already makes.[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Recolours, custom sprites and map mods work without being told about them, and every effect has its own switch.[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8][b]Needs[/b] SMAPI · [b]Optional[/b] Generic Mod Config Menu · [b]Runs on[/b] PC and Android
[b]Safe[/b] to add or remove mid-save · [b]F6[/b] opens the tuner[/color]

[size=3][color=#ff6b6b][b]Your settings now survive updates.[/b][/color][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]From 2.3.1 the mod keeps its own copy of your settings and brings them back after an update, even through Vortex ([url=https://github.com/Nexus-Mods/Vortex/issues/15419]which deletes a mod's config.json[/url]).
[b]Coming from 2.3.0 or older?[/b] That one update can still reset them: copy config.json first, or press [b]Copy everything[/b] in the F6 Looks tab and keep the code.[/color][/center]

[color=#D4D4D8][b]1.[/b] Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url].
[b]2.[/b] Unzip into your [font=Courier New]Mods[/font] folder. [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] is optional but recommended.
[b]3.[/b] Play, and press [b]F6[/b] in game to open the tuner. On a phone, open it from the config menu: SDV-Radiance, Hotkeys & diagnostics, Open the Radiance tuner.[/color]

[img]https://phuicmt.github.io/SDV-Radiance-media/banners/make-it-yours.png[/img]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]F6[/b] opens the live tuner: drag any slider and watch the world change, save your own looks, or start from Subtle, Cinematic, Vibrant or Nocturne. Share a look as a code and paste someone else's. Most settings are in Generic Mod Config Menu too, and its Open the Radiance tuner box opens the rest.[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8][b]Lighting and shadows[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Directional shadows[/b] cut from the real sprite silhouettes, leaning and stretching with the sun, [b]moonlight shadows[/b] at night by lunar phase, and [b]lamp shadows[/b] indoors from torches, lanterns and fireplaces: up to 48 lights light a scene, and the eight that matter most each throw a shadow of their own.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Shadows that read the light (new in 2.0.0).[/b] A shadow is no longer plain black: it takes the blue of a clear sky, the grey of rain or the warmth of a room (Shadow colour). It is sharp where a thing touches the ground and softens toward its tip, and its soft rim stretches along the shadow as the sun gets lower (Sharp where it touches, Soft edge follows the light).[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]A dark pool under people and animals (new in 2.0.0),[/b] so nobody looks like they are floating at noon, when the real shadow hides behind the body. It starts at 0.5. The same pool under trees and objects ships at zero.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Your sun, your way (new in 2.0.0).[/b] Sun direction turns where the sun passes at noon, and the light itself (sun shafts, lit sides, window daylight and water glitter) has its own Sun direction for the light, so the two can agree. The player, villagers, farm animals and other creatures each get their own shadow switch. Sun follows the season, for long winter shadows and short summer ones, ships off.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Bounced light that walls stop,[/b] worked out with radiance cascades so it reaches around a corner. Warm light pools around real sources and is blocked by what is in the way, so a flat interior gets depth.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Art that glows.[/b] A lit sign or a forge emits its own colour, and labelled windows glow after dusk and lay [b]daylight across the floor[/b] by hour, season and weather. Dappled sunlight reaches the greenhouse floor too, with its own Sun through a glass roof switch (new in 2.0.0).[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Nights with real lamps (new in 2.0.0).[/b] A lit window pushes the night back, so the street in front of a house shows its painted colour again. Every lamp wears a faint halo, embers, fireflies and chimney sparks light the wall beside them, a fish tank throws moving water light across the room, and the town's winter tree twinkles in colour.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Glass reflects, indoors too (new in 2.0.0).[/b] Windows return whoever stands in front of them. Inside, a window turns into a mirror of the room after dark, with its lamps standing in it. The bus at the bus stop and the bath house mirrors reflect too (new in 2.1.0), and a TV that is on lights the room like a screen (new in 2.1.0).[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Lightning is answered by the scene[/b]: shadows kick away from the bolt, the darkness lifts with the flash, a warm afterglow follows it.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]Water[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Two waters, your pick[/b]: Water 1.6 with its travelling ripple spectrum, depth fade and camera parallax, or Water 1.5 with its three looks. Each shows only its own dials.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Reflections along the real painted shoreline[/b], not the tile edge. Your own reflection follows you into the shallows, crab pots, splashes and the bobber reflect too, and a tree in the water leans with the tree on the bank.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Water that notices the world (new in 2.0.0).[/b] The wind carries the ripple downwind and scatters more glints in a gale, and a cloud passing over dims the sparkle. Ducks, waders and a landing cast leave rings behind them, and fish keep a bubbling spot stirred, harder in a frenzy. Glitter follows the sun, which draws the glints into a lane toward a low sun, ships off.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Rivers that flow (new in 2.1.0).[/b] A map that paints a waterfall has its river traced along its banks, and the surface is carried with it, quick at the foot of the fall and slower along the banks, with foam riding the current and rain swelling it. Pools the river passes stay still, and the sea gets its own wave dial. How the river looks is a group of dials of its own; River moves in pixel steps, for the game's own stepped look, ships off.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Caustics on the shallow bed, rain rings on the surface[/b], and ripple that knows a pond from an ocean, and summer from ice.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Detection from what the game actually draws[/b] plus a hand-painted label set, so modded water lines up. Ice, flowing water, waterfalls and lava each read differently.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]Weather, particles and colour[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Rain, snow and windblown leaves at three depths[/b], splashes where drops land, storm density and rain slant as dials, and [b]lightning you can see[/b] on any map.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Weather you can see coming (new in 2.0.0).[/b] The afternoon before a rainy day, cloud shadows gather and the light cools (Before the rain). Crops lean with the wind along with the trees and bushes, and snow glitters in the winter sun.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Drops on the edge of the screen[/b] that merge, grow heavy and run, becoming frost in snow.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Particles drawn into the world[/b]: dust in a window beam, sparks off the fire, fireflies, waterfall mist, hot-spring steam, lava sparks, and blossom and leaves that bend with the water's own wave.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]More small life in the world (new in 2.0.0).[/b] Dry dirt and sand lift a little dust under your feet and everyone else's, a chimney shimmers with heat and throws a spark or two after dark, mist drifts over a foggy mine level, a rainbow stands in waterfall spray when the sun is low enough for one, and watered soil sparkles in the sun.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Sun shafts cut from what actually blocks the light[/b], on by default. Lamp shafts are rebuilt the same way and ship off, as a taste.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Colour grading[/b] by time, weather and season with metered auto-exposure, six ready-made looks and a slot for your own LUT. [b]Ships off[/b]: the colour of somebody's game is not a thing to change unasked. A [b]blue light filter[/b] rides on top.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]And the rest[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Wind in the trees.[/b] Tree tops and bushes lean with the same wind the rain leans with, so a storm tips them further and a calm day barely moves them, and a gust front crosses the map so a row of trees leans one after another. What ships is a tilt of a fraction of a degree, because bending pixel art into a curve tears it. On by default.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Aurora on clear winter nights[/b], drawn into the sea as well as the sky, with a surge that runs along a curtain and dies. [b]Shooting stars[/b] cross over water. Both on, both rare enough to be worth looking up for.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Lamp shadows with shapes.[/b] Fences, bushes and boulders throw their own silhouette instead of a round patch, placed things block lamp light, and a shadow softens with distance from the lamp.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Shadow shapes, your pick.[/b] The shadows page opens with [b]Shadows 1.7[/b] or [b]Shadows 1.6[/b]. The newer shape stands a placed thing's shadow on the row its art really ends on and lays a horse, a pet or a wildlife mod's creature down across the ground. Shape only, fixes stay fixed under both.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Colour has its own glow.[/b] Bloom asks whether a pixel shines with a colour as well as whether it is bright, so lit panes and flames glow sooner while snow stays quiet.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Smoother art, if you want it.[/b] A diagonal edge in this game is a staircase of square pixels, and this rounds those steps into the line the artist drew, using only the colours already there. It ships off. Soft 4x can be made with xBR, MMPX or EPX [b](new in 2.2.0)[/b]. The world, the characters, the portraits, the items lying in the world and the menus each have their own switch and dial, so you can keep the dialogue text sharp and let the trees soften.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Sprite relief, off by default.[/b] A lamp lights the side of a tree, a building or a person that faces it a little more, read from the art's own outline and shading. It also carries the rim light that separates a person from the cobbles behind them at night, and leaves that brighten and dim as they flip in the wind.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Golden hour,[/b] its own warmth and long light for the twenty minutes either side of sundown, and bounced light that takes the colour of surfaces. Both ship at zero.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]The tuner hides what cannot work.[/b] A dial under a switch you turned off is not greyed out. It is gone, and the page regroups around what is left.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[color=#D4D4D8][b]Performance.[/b] One shader chain on the frame the game already drew, cached between frames. What it costs depends on your machine, every part has a switch that gives its cost back, and [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] prints the breakdown for yours.[/color]
[spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]Everything here is developed and tested on one machine,[/b] a Core Ultra 7 with an RTX 5080, playing at 3440x1369 with zoom at 0.75. That is worth knowing before you take anything I say about speed at face value, because a number from my machine says very little about yours. The numbers in the release notes above come from my machine too. So rather than lean on them, measure it. [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] prints the cost line by line, for your machine, in the scene you are standing in, and the Performance tab has a ten-second benchmark that needs nothing switched on first. If something reads as expensive there, say so on the Posts tab with that output and it gets looked at.

[b]What to reach for if it runs badly.[/b] The Performance tab has four presets and an effect resolution slider, and no preset lowers that resolution on its own any more, because the round trip softened every sprite. The biggest single saving is Flood GI lighting off, on the Dynamic lighting page. Next is Lamp shadow detail at 0 on the same page, then object shadows. Shadows-per-character is the most direct lever after those, and the lamp shadows and their softness each switch off on their own. [b]Switching an effect off gives its cost back[/b], which is measured rather than assumed: with every feature off, what is left is close to nothing.

[b]Every speed change has a way back, live, while the game runs.[/b] [font=Courier New]radiance_samplerslots full[/font] puts the driver's texture slot list back, [font=Courier New]radiance_reliefsort depth[/font] and [font=Courier New]radiance_reliefres full[/font] draw the sprite relief the way earlier versions did, [font=Courier New]radiance_marchcache off[/font] walks every lamp's shadow fresh again, and [font=Courier New]radiance_sheetread strips[/font] reads sheets back the old way. [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] says which of them is in force, where your frame is going, how many updates the game ran for each frame it drew, and what every cache is holding.[/color]
[/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]Compatibility[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Appearance mods just work[/b]: everything is generated from what is actually rendered. Tested alongside SVE and 80+ mod setups.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Cloudy Skies and Weather Wonders[/b] share the weather with this mod frame by frame. On a day they draw their own custom weather this mod steps aside, and on an ordinary rainy or snowy day its own rain and snow show. A weather mod that replaces the game's weather drawing outright still gets it to itself for the whole session.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Map screenshots[/b] (the game's Screenshot button, Daily Screenshot) save the game's normal picture, or the picture with this mod's effects once [b]Effects in map screenshots[/b] is on in the Camera tab.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Global God Rays[/b]: works together. The two cover similar ground, so run both and turn one down, or run either.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Multiplayer and split screen[/b]: client-side, only you need it. Other players cast shadows and reflect, and each screen keeps its own data.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]SpriteMaster / Clear Glasses: pick one.[/b] Smooth art steps aside for them by itself, but shadows and water can still flicker next to Clear Glasses. [b]Clear Monocle works.[/b] DynamicShader works alongside. With ReShade or another post-processing mod the effects stack, so turn one of them down. [b]Android[/b]: runs through SMAPI for Android. 2.2.9 loads on phones again and brings the phone fixes from 2.2.8 with it. I cannot test on a phone myself, so reports from phones are very welcome.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8][b]Known issues[/b][/color]
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Map screenshots with effects have no drifting particles yet:[/b] the mist puffs at the falls, leaves, fireflies and dust are left out. Everything else is in them.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]A shadow can fall across a table or a counter it should stop at.[/b] The pass knows what blocks light on the ground, not what stands on top of furniture.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Some glass does not reflect yet.[/b] Glass the mod does not recognise shows nothing in it. If you find some, a screenshot and where it was is all I need.[/color][/*]

[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Online co-op has had less testing than split screen.[/b] The code is shared, the two-machine session is not. [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] plus [font=Courier New]radiance_screenwatch[/font] collect what I need.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Smooth art uses video memory.[/b] The soft look bakes its sprites onto pages of up to 192 MB, and [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] lists what every cache is holding. If your card is short of memory, turning Smooth art off gives it back.[/color][/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

Downloads.Description: Your settings now survive updates. Snow mods like Fluttery Flakes keep their snow near water, tree shadows grow from the roots, three looks for drops on the glass, Junimo and fence shadow settings.

Manifest.Name: SDV-Radiance
Manifest.Description: Graphics suite for Stardew Valley: bloom, color grading, sun shafts, fog, cloud & directional shadows, lamp shadows with real shapes, water reflections, window reflections, wind in the trees, aurora and shooting stars, particles, layered rain and snow, and occlusion-aware GI lighting.
